newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end lower in quiet Easter trading.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end lower in quiet Easter trading.

text.p: Milan shares remained in negative territory all Friday and ended lower reflecting the overnight tumble to U.S. stocks while there was little trading interest in the market with most of Europe and the U.S. on holiday.

With bonds and the lira generally easier there was no reason for investors to buy amid worries on how Wall Street might open next week. Milan was one of only a few bourses open on Good Friday but it will be closed on Easter Monday.
Blue-chip Mib30 index ended 1.91 percent lower at 17,461, while all-share Mibtel index closed 1.61 percent off at 11,830.
Many blue chips down in line with the market with ENI off 1.88 percent at 8,460 lire, Fiat off 2,38 percent at 5,300 lire and Pirelli down 3.29 percent at 3,641 lire.

Fiat controlled groups Snia BPD and Snia Fibre were suspended today ahead of a statement which later said the share exchange ratio for the merger of the two groups would be two ordinary BPD shares for five Fibre shares.
Among the smaller stocks, automobile brake manufacturer Brembo was suspended 10 percent limit down after announcing lower 1996 profits and a steady dividend.
